steps.speaker: Message
steps.content: Alert, there has been an explosion in the kitchen. Suspect: Ignis.
The floor is shaking a little, unexpected but not nothing outrageous.
By the time you rush into the kitchen, the fire is already out.
Ignis is holding a fire extinguisher and standing in the messy kitchen. Her hair full of powder—she may not know how to use a fire extinguisher.

options: Whoa. It's just one thing after another.

choices.text: Whoa. It's just one thing after another.

steps.content: She is angry and nervous. It seems like her MBCC prison education didn't teach her the vulgar language to handle a situation like this.
You parted on bad terms last time, and it is still awkward between the two of you.
This seems like a fine opportunity to reconcile.
You walk over to help her clean. Ignis starts, but she does not run away.
Maybe she was also waiting for an opportunity like this.
Meals at the Bureau are alright, why did you come to the kitchen to get more?
Did you not like the food today?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Ah... That's not it...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I just wasn't that full... That's all.
She is probably really hungry.
You suddenly think, a colleague told you that they missed lunch.

options: Do you want some grilled steak?
Can you help me cut up this steak then?

choices.text: Do you want some grilled steak?
Can you help me cut up this steak then?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I'm not that hungry.
Really?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: If you really want to make some... then... I could eat.
So help me cut up this steak.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Why would I...
So you don't want any?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: If you really want to make some for me... I might as well help out!
Ignis's gaze is unsteady, and she won't look at you.
But, she takes the steak and silently walks over to a surviving counter off to one side, and starts cutting. The rock-hard frozen meat becomes more pliable in her hands.
Your knife skills aren't bad. And you can defrost too.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I was always responsible for the cold dishes at the restaurant, so... I'm alright at it.
You're very good with that knife. I feel like an amateur.
Ignis looks at you, her knife never stopping.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Of course. The cold dishes at the restaurant were always my responsibility.
Talking about her past, Ignis's mood seems to be improving.
So, apart from writing the blog, you worked in your parents' restaurant?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: ...Sort of.
What do you mean "sort of"?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I don't want to say.
Ignis cut the steak and doesn't talk anymore. You can tell she means it.
It's okay if you don't want to say.
Oh, are you done with the steak? Can you help me with the soup?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: No, I don't want to.
Why?
Ignis puts down the kitchen knife, taking a quick glance at you. Her face is turning red.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: If I tell you, don't laugh.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: When I'm around fire, I can't control my own fire, so...
So the renowned gourmand Crème Brûlée actually can't cook.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: It's not that I can't cook! You... You're laughing at me!

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Hey! You're cutting the onions crooked!

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: How dare you laugh at me!
You clear your throat and stop laughing.
You're seeing things.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: This is the first time I've met a chief who can talk such nonsense without even blushing.
You cough, embarrassed.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Hmph.
So you only made cold dishes in your parents' restaurant, and never went in the kitchen.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Okay.
Are your parents alright? Do they still run the restaurant?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: They...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Are you trying to get information out of me? I don't want to talk about them.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Last time I told you, I am me, and they are them. Nothing I've done has anything to do with them.
The FAC didn't sell out anyone.
I didn't mean anything by it, and I won't break any promises I've already made. I just want to understand you a little better.
After all, we're going to be comrades-in-arms, living and dying together.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: ...Okay.
She looks hesitant but makes her mind to say "okay".
She takes a deep breath.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: This was my condition when I turned myself in to the FAC.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I would go along with their investigation and do whatever they wanted, as long as they protected my parents and kept them from being implicated in the fire.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: You know what it's like in Eastside for the families of Sinners...
I know. That was very thoughtful of you.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: It was one of the only things I could do for them.
You wanted to sacrifice yourself to make it up to them?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: They always made sacrifices for me.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Before I burned down the restaurant when I was six, they had steady work, steady incomes.
This isn't your fault, Ignis.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: It is my fault. There isn't anyone else to blame.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: When I revealed my ability, they left their jobs, sold the house to pay back the restaurant owner, and we had to move to an anonymous corner of Eastside, all for me. It was always like that—if I carelessly exposed my ability, it was time to drop everything, change schools, move house.
Ignis puts down the kitchen knife and sighs.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: They even... To make it easier to move, my dad traded our little car for a pickup truck, and we used folding cots for beds because they were easier to pack up. There was always a surveillance camera on the door so that no one could barge in without us knowing.

options: Your parents loved you very much.

choices.text: Your parents loved you very much.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: After that, my parents never had steady work. They were always taking care of things for me, and filled the house with fire safety equipment.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I didn't dare go outside to play with anyone, so they bought me lots of books. I couldn't cook, so my mother encouraged me to write a food blog.
You were wondering how she was able to continue to suffer in silence, and now you have the answer.
It was because Ignis's parents were always behind her.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I hadn't been a normal kid since I was little. I never had a chance to get close to the other children at school. Someone would bully me, and I'd lose control and expose my ability. My parents were also my only friends.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I was terrified to be exposed, so I deliberately treat people coldly just to alienate everyone. Even when I was bullied, I only gritted my teeth and not say a word. But the more I be like this, the more people isolate and bully me...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: When I was 14, I started writing the blog, and my ability stabilized for a bit. We thought a new life was beginning.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Only my parents. They are my only friends.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: My parents saved up to renovate the restaurant for the official opening at the gourmet festival. I picked out every table, every chair, every tablecloth, and every decorative painting there.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: It's all gone now because of me. All the improved business, the happy life, the bright future... Everything's gone.
I am so sorry...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: It was all because of me. I got carried away online. I shouldn't have gone chasing after things I didn't deserve. It was all my fault...
You didn't do anything wrong, you couldn't have predicted those crazy fans.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: No, I should have known. I realized that day that as long as I was a ticking time bomb, their lives would never get better.
It's not your fault, it's not anyone's fault. You didn't make bad things happen to them, they just happened.
Your parents wouldn't want you to carry this pain all alone. You are family, and when bad things happen, family faces it together.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: No...
What if I told you that your parents never blamed you, and that they were completely against the FAC's intervention? That they hope to someday take you back?
A year ago, they opened a new shop. Sure, they had a setback, but your parents didn't stop trying. They pulled themselves back up and kept going.

options: Your loved ones are not that fragile.
You don't have to put yourself down.

choices.text: Your loved ones are not that fragile.
You don't have to put yourself down.

steps.content: You don't have to shut yourself away completely because you're afraid of hurting people. Leaving only hurts both you and them.
Ignis, do you want to go back home?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Haha...
All of her struggling ends with a sigh, a chuckle. She raises her head to look you straight in the eyes. For the first time, you see her smile, and it is difficult to take.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I won't go back.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I already know everything you've been telling me. Nightingale tells me what I want to know privately. She's a busybody like you.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I know how depressed they were, and that they rejected FAC's protection many times, because FAC took me away.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I also know that they have slowly gotten happier, received help, paid off their debts, opened a new shop, and come out of the shadows to start a new life.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, do you know what the turning point was?
You shake your head. The quiet air is getting more uncomfortable.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: My mother and father have a new daughter.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Not like me: an ordinary daughter, a normal family member.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: They told me her name is Elise.
The air grows thick. You can barely look at her.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: ...What's that look on your face? It's annoying.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I... I'm fine. I'm very happy. I can't be a little kid forever, and they've done enough for me.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I always wanted them to be happy and start a new life.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: And you see, as soon as they moved on from me, my wish came true.
She is still smiling, and the tears in her eyes haven't fallen.
